data.name: Tip_Locations

Leave a box empty to keep the auto-detect for it. With the game, mods and profiles folders typed, ModOrganizer.ini isn't needed.

data.name: Mo2_InfoDefault
data.value: Reads your mods directly. No need to launch AnvilLOD from MO2.

data.name: Locations_PopupHint

data.name: Timing_TreesFmt

data.name: Tip_Print
data.value: Saves what this tab shows to a file (Overview and Log as text, Blocks and Missing meshes as CSV) so you can read it later.

data.name: Tip_Expand
data.value: Fills the window with this box. Press again (or Esc) to bring the options back.

data.name: Tip_PresetFmt
data.value: Preset {0}. Each preset remembers every setting in this column. Click to switch, double-click to rename.

data.name: CatOutput_Desc
data.value: Where the LOD goes, which worldspaces and which LOD levels to build.

data.name: Tip_OutputBox
data.value: Where LOD files go. Leave it empty to use 'AnvilLOD Output' (a new mod folder in the MO2 mods folder, Vortex's staging folder, or Documents). The folder is created if it doesn't exist.

data.name: Opt_CleanOutput
data.value: Empty the output folder before generating

data.name: Tip_CleanOutput
data.value: Deletes what the last run left in the output folder first, so old files never mix with the new ones. Only done in an empty folder or one AnvilLOD wrote (it has AnvilLOD.manifest.json or AnvilLOD.log); any other folder is left alone and the log says so. MO2's meta.ini is kept. Every block is written again each run; untick to update the folder in place and only rewrite what changed.

data.name: Tip_WorldspaceBox
data.value: Comma separated EditorIDs, e.g. Tamriel, DLC2SolstheimWorld

data.name: CatRules_Desc
data.value: Which LOD model or billboard each kind of object uses at each LOD level. AnvilLOD reuses DynDOLOD rule files.

data.name: Tip_DynDolodBox
data.value: Folder with DynDOLODx64.exe. Its rule files plus the ones mods ship in Data\DynDOLOD decide which LOD mesh each object uses.

data.name: Tip_EditRules
data.value: Look at and change the LOD rules of this preset: which LOD model or billboard each kind of object uses at each LOD level. Your changes are saved as your own rule file.

data.name: Tip_Candles
data.value: Also load DynDOLOD's Candles rules for this preset: candles, lanterns and sconces get Far LOD, so their light shows in the distance. Needs the DynDOLOD folder.

data.name: Tip_FxGlow
data.value: Also load DynDOLOD's FXGlow rules for this preset: the glow cards of fires and lights get Far LOD. Needs the DynDOLOD folder.

data.name: Tip_CustomRulesCheck
data.value: Use this rule file. Its rules come before DynDOLOD's own and win. Unticked: only DynDOLOD's own rule files are used.

data.name: Tip_CustomRulesBox
data.value: A rule file in DynDOLOD's format: one saved from Edit rules, or a DynDOLOD preset or rule file you have. Tick the box to use it.

data.name: CatObjects_Desc
data.value: Object LOD, PBR, brightness, terrain underside, large references and which references count.

data.name: Tip_RemoveBuried
data.value: Drops LOD triangles that are completely underground. Big savings on mountains and rocks.

data.name: Opt_PbrLod
data.value: Match PBR textures in object LOD

data.name: Tip_PbrLod
data.value: LOD uses vanilla shaders, so a LOD mesh that uses a texture your PBR mods replace shows the vanilla look while the real object shows the PBR one (mountains, buildings). With this on, LOD textures that TexGen made a pbr_lod twin of use the twin, and other textures that have a PBR version (textures\pbr\...) use a darkened, shrunk copy of the PBR albedo written to textures\anvillod\pbr. Changing it or the brightness rebuilds every block.

data.name: Opt_PbrBrightness
data.value: PBR LOD texture brightness (1.0 = DynDOLOD default)

data.name: Tip_PbrBrightness
data.value: Brightness of the converted PBR copies, as a share of DynDOLOD's default PBR scale. Lower it if the LOD looks brighter than the real objects.

data.name: Tip_LargeRefs
data.value: The engine's large reference grid (uLargeRefLODGridSize in SkyrimPrefs.ini) shows the full models of listed references beyond the loaded cells. Skyrim.esm and the DLCs list theirs; this lists the qualifying references from your other ESM-flagged plugins that nobody lists yet, in AnvilLOD.esm, flagged ESL (no plugin slot). Enable it after your other ESMs. References that a plugin outside the ESMs overrides or that start disabled are left out, because those make large references flicker. The report says what was listed and what was left out.

data.name: Opt_LargeRefsEsl
data.value: Flag AnvilLOD.esm as ESL (saves a plugin slot)

data.name: Tip_LargeRefsEsl
data.value: On: the plugin is flagged ESL and takes no plugin slot. Off: it is a normal ESM that uses a slot. If large references flicker at a distance, you can untick this to rule the ESL flag out, at the cost of one slot.

data.name: Opt_LargeRefsEslNote
data.value: Flagging it ESL saves a plugin slot. If large references flicker at a distance, untick it to use a normal ESM slot instead.

data.name: Tip_Underside
data.value: Builds a low-resolution, downward-facing copy of the terrain (meshes\Terrain\<worldspace>\<worldspace>_Underside.nif) and AnvilLOD.esp, flagged ESL, that places it 500 units below the world. DVLaSS, EVLaS and Community Shaders' sky sync use it to stop sun rays and shadows leaking through the landscape. Enable the plugin in your mod manager and load it after plugins that edit worldspaces. Do not use it together with DynDOLOD's own underside.

data.name: Opt_ObjectBrightness
data.value: Object LOD brightness (buildings, rocks, grass LOD)

data.name: Tip_ObjectBrightness
data.value: Darkens object LOD through vertex colours, so the LOD textures themselves (shared with other mods) are left alone. Changing it rebuilds every block.

data.name: Opt_IncludeEnableParent
data.value: Include enable-parented references that start enabled

data.name: Tip_IncludeEnableParent
data.value: Parented references that start disabled (quest-built or rebuilt places such as Helgen Reborn) are always left out of static LOD.

data.name: CatTrees_Desc
data.value: Billboard tree LOD and 3D tree LOD models.

data.name: Tip_TreeLod
data.value: Builds the engine's billboard tree LOD (.lst, .btt and the tree atlas) from textures\terrain\LODGen billboards, e.g. TexGen output.

data.name: Tip_TreeBrightness
data.value: Darkens or brightens the distant tree billboards to match your lighting/ENB.

data.name: Tip_Tree3D
data.value: Trees that have a 3D tree LOD model (DynDOLOD's passthru_lod.nif, found by the CRC32 of the tree's mesh) go into object LOD: the 3D model at LOD4, billboard cards from LOD8 on. Trees without a model keep the billboard tree LOD. Needs the models' textures, including the trunk billboards TexGen renders.

data.name: Opt_Tree3DLod8
data.value: Also use the 3D models at LOD8

data.name: Tip_Tree3DLod8
data.value: Nicer mid-distance trees, but much bigger LOD files. Off: 3D at LOD4 only, cards from LOD8.

data.name: Opt_Tree3DByName
data.value: Accept models by tree name (DynDOLOD's default)

data.name: Tip_Tree3DByName
data.value: DynDOLOD Resources ships almost all 3D tree models under the plain tree name; a CRC32 in the name is only for name collisions, and DynDOLOD itself matches by name. On (default): a model stored under the plain tree name is used when no CRC32-named one exists. Off: only exact CRC32 matches are used, which finds none with DynDOLOD Resources. A model made for another version of a tree mesh (before a mod or PGPatcher changed it) can look slightly off.

data.name: CatGrass_Desc
data.value: Distant grass from your grass cache. This is the biggest choice for file size, disk space and graphics load.

data.name: Tip_GrassLod
data.value: Adds distant grass to the LOD4 blocks from your NGIO/FasterNGIO grass cache, textured with TexGen grass billboards.

data.name: Tip_GrassDensity
data.value: Share of the cached grass kept as LOD tufts, spread evenly over the ground. More is fuller and closer to the real grass, but makes bigger files and more triangles to draw. The sizes listed are for a large load order's Tamriel (object LOD, normal grass cache). Seasons of Skyrim adds a full set per season, and summer's grass cache is much denser than winter's, so seasonal output is several times bigger.

data.name: Opt_GrassBrightness
data.value: Grass LOD brightness: top of the tufts / roots

data.name: Tip_GrassTop
data.value: How bright the top of each grass tuft is (like DynDOLOD's GrassBrightnessTop). Lower it if distant grass looks brighter than the real grass. Changing it rebuilds the grass blocks.

data.name: Tip_GrassBottom
data.value: How bright the roots are (like DynDOLOD's GrassBrightnessBottom). A darker root fakes the shadow inside the grass. Changing it rebuilds the grass blocks.

data.name: Estimate_Default
data.value: Generate once and AnvilLOD can estimate the size of your next generation from your own list.

data.name: Estimate_Guide
data.value: As a guide for one big worldspace without seasons: grass at 4% is about 0.7 GB, 15% about 1.7 GB, 40% about 3.9 GB and 100% about 11 GB. Seasons add a full copy of the changed blocks for each season (summer is the biggest, its grass cache is much denser).

data.name: Estimate_Tip
data.value: Tip: set this to the most your PC can really run, not the maximum on offer. Grass, trees and seasons multiply each other, so a higher setting than your graphics card or memory can use only costs disk space, load time and frame rate. If in doubt, generate at a lower density first: the in-game Quality Layers menu can lower the load later, but cannot make a file smaller.

data.name: CatDynamic_Desc
data.value: Seasons of Skyrim LOD, the SKSE plugin, quest-switched references, water and animated objects.

data.name: Tip_DynamicLod
data.value: References that quests enable or disable (Helgen Reborn's destroyed/rebuilt town, for example) get no static LOD. The AnvilLOD SKSE plugin shows their LOD only while they're enabled.

data.name: Tip_GridObjects
data.value: Water planes, waterfalls, creeks, fires, windmills and ships (DynDOLOD 'grid' objects, from the rules' Grid column) are drawn beyond the loaded cells by the AnvilLOD SKSE plugin, with their animations. Uses DynDOLOD's _dyndolod_lod meshes when a mod ships them.

data.name: Opt_WaterStandIns
data.value: Stream, creek and pond water stand-ins

data.name: Tip_WaterStandIns
data.value: Stream, creek and pond water planes (Water1024Creek, the tundra stream pieces and the like) use a real water shader, which draws black beyond the loaded cells. This writes a lit, semi-transparent 'fake water' copy of each into the output (meshes\anvillod\water) and has the SKSE plugin draw that instead, the way CS Water Mod's own stream twins look. The sea and big lakes come from terrain LOD (xLODGen) and are not affected. Needs 'Water and animated distant objects' ticked. The original meshes are not changed.

data.name: Tip_Seasons
data.value: For powerof3's Seasons of Skyrim: writes seasonal object LOD (*.WIN.bto, *.SUM.bto, ...) for every season that has form-swap INIs in Data\Seasons. Swapped objects use their swap's LOD; unchanged blocks are hard links, so little extra disk space. Tree and terrain LOD stay the same in every season.

data.name: Tip_SkseDll
data.value: Puts the AnvilLOD SKSE plugin into the output folder so the LOD output is a single install. Auto-detect reads the version of SkyrimSE.exe (or SkyrimVR.exe). Pick 'Installed separately' if you use the AnvilLOD SKSE Plugin FOMOD instead (don't have both).

data.name: Warning_Generated
data.value: These files are generated automatically from the mod's own models and textures. They are a starting point: check them in NifSkope and in game before using them, and only share them with the mod author's permission.

data.name: Finder_Description
data.value: Finds the objects and trees of one plugin that are seen from afar but have no LOD (no LOD mesh, a broken MNAM path, missing LOD textures, no tree billboard) and can generate them: simplified name_lod_0/1/2.nif, TexGen-style billboards and a DynDOLOD-format rule file. Everything goes into its own folder, never into your LOD output.

data.name: Agree_Text
data.value: I understand. Generated files are a starting point that I check before using, and I only share them with the mod author's permission.

data.name: Tip_AuthorPlugin
data.value: The plugin to check, e.g. The Archwood.esp

data.name: Tip_AuthorOut
data.value: Defaults to mods\AnvilLOD Author - <plugin> in your MO2 instance

data.name: Tip_AuthorMeshes
data.value: Simplified name_lod_0/1/2.nif for big objects without LOD

data.name: Tip_AuthorBillboards
data.value: TexGen-style billboards (.dds + .txt) for trees and big plants without one

data.name: Tip_AuthorRules
data.value: DynDOLOD\DynDOLOD_SSE_<plugin>.ini for the generated meshes (works with AnvilLOD and DynDOLOD)

data.name: Tip_Overwrite
data.value: Off: files already in the output folder (maybe hand-edited) are kept

data.name: Tip_AuthorBudget
data.value: Keeps each generated LOD mesh within the triangles that SE/AE LOD meshes of the same size use (measured from DynDOLOD Resources SE and LOD Model Library). Off: only the simplifier's error limit applies, so dense models stay heavy.

data.name: Finder_TreesFrom
data.value: units; trees need a billboard from

data.name: Tip_AuthorCheck
data.value: Report only, nothing is written except the report

data.name: Author_ListFailedFmt
data.value: Couldn't list plugins (type the name instead): {0}

data.name: Author_CheckedFmt
data.value: {0} placed objects/trees checked: {1} missing LOD or billboards, {2} with broken files.

data.name: Maker_Description
data.value: Makes LOD meshes (name_lod_0/1/2.nif) from full models you pick: small parts are dropped, the rest is simplified, the model's own textures are kept and collision is not copied. A DynDOLOD-format rule file makes AnvilLOD and DynDOLOD use them. It only reads the model files, so it needs no load order.

data.name: Maker_Models
data.value: Models (one per line: a .nif, a mod folder, its meshes folder, or any folder of models)

data.name: Tip_MakerInput
data.value: Folders are searched for .nif files (inside their meshes folder if they have one). Models that are already LOD meshes are skipped.

data.name: Maker_NewMod
data.value: A new mod in my MO2 mods folder (needs MO2 instance mode above)

data.name: Tip_MakerModName
data.value: Becomes mods\<name> in your MO2 instance. Run it again with the same name to add more models to it.

data.name: Maker_ChooseFolder
data.value: A folder I choose (new or existing)

data.name: Tip_MakerOut
data.value: Use a separate folder, not your LOD output folder

data.name: Tip_MakerDetail
data.value: How much is removed. A finer setting keeps more triangles. Very dense models stay heavy at the normal setting: use a coarser one.

data.name: Tip_MakerMinSize
data.value: Largest dimension in game units. 0 = make LOD for every model you picked.

data.name: Tip_MakerBudget
data.value: Recommended: a budget for each level that grows with the model's size, taken from the LOD meshes SE/AE lists already use. Custom: your own maximums. Off: only the Detail setting limits the triangles.

data.name: Tip_MakerBudget0
data.value: Most triangles at LOD 0 (0 = no limit)

data.name: Tip_MakerBudget1
data.value: Most triangles at LOD 1 (0 = no limit)

data.name: Tip_MakerBudget2
data.value: Most triangles at LOD 2 (0 = no limit)

data.name: Maker_HintRecommended
data.value: Most triangles at LOD 0 / 1 / 2, by the model's largest dimension: {0}. Based on the {1}.

data.name: Maker_HintCustom
data.value: Your own maximums per level; 0 means no limit for that level. A farther level never gets more triangles than a nearer one.

data.name: Maker_HintOff
data.value: No budget: only the Detail setting limits the triangles, so very dense models stay heavy.

data.name: Tip_MakerRules
data.value: DynDOLOD\DynDOLOD_SSE_<name>.ini so the meshes are used for the models they were made from. An existing file only gets lines for new models.

data.name: Maker_SummaryFmt
data.value: {0} models done, {1} LOD meshes written{2}{3}. Output: {4}. Report: {5}

data.value: Show only rules whose mesh mask, FormID or file name contains this text

data.value: Replace your custom rules with the rules of a DynDOLOD-format rule file.

data.name: Tip_DialogMask
data.value: A mesh mask, 'Path\To\Model.nif' or part of the path of the full model a base record uses (tree, \road, rtkeep), or the FormID of a reference or base record, 'Plugin.esp;000F64BF'. The catch-all rule is a single backslash.

data.name: Dialog_MaskHelp
data.value: Mesh mask: part of the full model's path. Reference FormID: Plugin.esp;FormID of a reference or base record. A single \ is the catch-all rule (always applied last).

data.name: Dialog_FlagVwd
data.value: VWD - Visible When Distant: apply the rule only if a matching LOD model exists

data.name: Dialog_FlagNoGlow
data.value: NoGlow - no glowing windows (saved in the file; AnvilLOD does not apply it yet)

data.name: Dialog_FlagNoMato
data.value: NoMATO - no material object shader: do not apply it to the LOD model

data.name: Dialog_FlagDynamic
data.value: Dynamic - force dynamic LOD: adds both dynamic LOD and the object LOD model

data.name: Dialog_FlagTree

data.name: Dialog_LevelHelp
data.value: Level0 = the LOD4 model, Level1 = LOD8, Level2 = LOD16. BillboardN = a tree billboard. Full model = the object's own model. None = no LOD at this level.

data.name: Dialog_GridHelp
data.value: Grid: water, fires, windmills and other objects that only get dynamic LOD (Near LOD, Far LOD, Far Full). The Reference column is saved in the file but AnvilLOD does not act on it yet.

data.name: Msg_RuleNeedsMask
data.value: The rule needs a mesh mask or a reference FormID.
